name: Web backup archives
description: Versioned ZIP archives of a published site directory, plus dated packages for operational handover: reproducible artefacts, documented exclusions, and no credentials in the archive.
longDescription: Dated ZIP archives stored next to a published static or PHP site directory so teams can compare, restore, or audit deployments. Packaging follows exclusion rules for large binaries and keeps credentials and internal server paths out of the archive. Backups are treated as a security object, not only a recovery object.
technologies: Published static and PHP site directory
features: Dated archive artefacts for point-in-time recovery
Site directory kept beside archives for comparison
Exclusion patterns for large binaries where appropriate
Guidance on what must never enter a shared archive
highlights: Operational maturity around verifiable point-in-time site archives
Useful for migration, compliance, and audit conversations
Security-conscious packaging with documented exclusion rules
challenges: Backups can accidentally include secrets if entire directories are archived without rules.
solutions: Document exclusions for environment files and private keys; prefer sanitized exports for sharing.
security: Keep credentials out of packaged directories
Encrypt offline backups on removable media
